note.text: Agglomeration is the concentration of related firms and supporting activities. Shared suppliers, specialist workers, infrastructure and knowledge can reduce costs or improve coordination. A cluster is not simply any large city. Congestion, expensive land and pollution can create diseconomies. Benefits depend on actual links, capacity and management; clustering does not guarantee success.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to explain a cluster benefit and a possible cost using evidence. Builds on: manufacturing inputs and services. Leads to: industrial development and location.

sections.heading: Follow the local example or model
sections.text: Uganda Investment Authority lists industrial parks including Jinja. A serviced park can bring firms near shared infrastructure, but a proposed advantage is not proof of every firm’s performance. The historic Zollverein complex at Essen in Germany illustrates links between production, rail and worker settlements in an older industrial region. These are different contexts, not identical development paths.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Identify what is shared and explain the mechanism. Then ask whether congestion or pressure on services could offset the saving. Separate a planned park, an operating cluster and a historical industrial landscape.

cards.idea: Distinguish the features before applying them.
example: supplier linkage: nearby firms supplying inputs or specialist services.
labour pool: a concentration of workers with relevant skills.
shared infrastructure: facilities serving several activities.
agglomeration diseconomy: a cost caused by excessive concentration or pressure.

cards.idea: Use the evidence in the example, not a place name alone.

Several workshops recruit locally trained technicians.
Firms use a common serviced access road.
Delivery vehicles lose time in congestion.

w: Every firm must make the same product

pick.r: Delivery delays may offset some shared-service savings
w: Congestion is proof of lower journey time
Only the number of buildings matters
e: Congestion adds delay.
Links and performance matter as well as buildings.
Shared facilities do not eliminate all costs.
pick.y: Evaluate both external economies and diseconomies.

w: The place has no service needs
e: The map alone does not show purchases.
Profit needs financial evidence.
Concentrated activity still needs services.
pick.y: Do not infer every cluster benefit from proximity alone.
